correctness.rationale: For all r>1 the two error norms follow from exact rank-one projectors. The surrogate singular values give the precise spectral scaling operators P1 and P2. The B^T B invariants are T=(r²+3)/2 and D=2r²/(r²+1); 1-T+D=-(r²-1)²/(2(r²+1))<0 ensures the singular values straddle 1. The exact identity T²-D(r+1/r)²=(r²-1)²/4>0 proves strict worsening, and the asymptotics follow from the quadratic formula. Reconstructed calculations and packaged checker were executed.

value.rationale: The problem is motivated by adaptive low-rank preconditioner rank selection: better low-rank approximations are often expected to make preconditioning safer. The theorem separates spectral and Frobenius surrogate accuracy from actual right-preconditioned conditioning with explicit natural singular-level targets, giving a strict all-r>1 reversal and an unbounded worst-case penalty. This is a substantive warning for rank-selection policies rather than a routine numerical example.
